issues.title: Hardcoded devtools loading message text
issues.description: The rule requires all user-facing strings to be defined in web/i18n/en-US/ translation files and accessed via useTranslation hook. The code hardcodes 'Loading devtools...' directly in the JSX instead of using a translation key.
issues.rule_name: Frontend User-Facing Strings Must Use i18n Translations

issues.title: Devtools rendered before application children causes layout issues
issues.description: The TanStackDevtoolsLoader is now rendered before the children components in the QueryClientProvider. This reverses the intended rendering order from the original PR, which had devtools after children. When devtools mount first, they may inject DOM elements before the main application content is rendered, potentially causing layout shifts, visual flashes, or z-index conflicts. Devtools should be rendered as a sibling after main content to avoid interfering with the initial application layout and rendering.

issues.title: Missing error logging in TanStack devtools lazy import
issues.description: The TanStackDevtoolsLoader silently swallows import errors without logging them, making it impossible to debug why the devtools fail to load. This creates an inconsistent error handling pattern compared to the ReactScanLoader (in the same PR), which properly logs errors with console.error before returning a fallback component. When developers encounter issues with TanStack devtools not appearing, they will have no visibility into whether it's due to an import failure, missing dependencies, or other issues.

issues.title: console.error violates Frontend Code Must Not Use console Statements rule
issues.description: The ReactScanLoader uses console.error which directly violates Rule 25 from AGENTS.md added in this same PR. The rule explicitly states that production frontend code must avoid console.log, console.warn, and console.error statements as enforced by the no-console warning rule. This creates an inconsistency where the code violates a compliance rule that was just introduced, and creates inconsistent error handling compared to TanStackDevtoolsLoader which silently catches errors. The use of console statements in production code should be replaced with proper logging mechanisms.

issues.title: console.error used in frontend code
issues.description: Rule 25 prohibits console statements in frontend code. The added code logs an error with console.error when lazy-loading fails.
issues.rule_name: Frontend Code Must Not Use console Statements

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30318 - refactor(web): organize devtools components

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves the two devtools integrations (React Scan and the TanStack devtools) into `web/app/components/devtools/{react-scan,tanstack}/`. Each folder gets a `loader.tsx` that checks `IS_DEV`, lazy-loads the tool and wraps it in `Suspense`. `layout.tsx` now renders `ReactScanLoader`, and `query-client.tsx` renders `TanStackDevtoolsLoader` instead of doing its own lazy loading.

Overall the change is good. The biggest gain is that `react-scan` was previously a static import in the root layout. It's now behind a dynamic import that runs only in development. There are a few small problems:
- The React Scan loader shows a visible "Loading devtools..." `<div>` as its Suspense fallback, placed at the very top of `<body>`. The tool itself renders nothing, so this placeholder is pure layout noise.
- The two loaders handle import failures differently: one logs the error, the other silently returns `null`.
- The PR description mentions an `index.ts` barrel file, but no such file exists.
structured_output.verdictRationale: This is a low-risk, dev-only refactor that also cuts react-scan from the production bundle. The issues found are minor: a cosmetic fallback, inconsistent error logging, and a description that doesn't match the code. None of them blocks merge.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `app/layout.tsx` statically imported `ReactScan` from `components/react-scan.tsx`, so `react-scan` was bundled in every build even though it only ran when `IS_DEV` was true. `context/query-client.tsx` handled lazy loading of the TanStack devtools inline (`lazy` + `Suspense` + `IS_DEV`), importing from `components/devtools.tsx`.

After this PR, each tool lives in its own folder with two files: an implementation file (`scan.tsx` / `devtools.tsx`, moved unchanged) and a `loader.tsx`. The loader returns `null` outside dev and otherwise lazy-imports the implementation inside a `Suspense` boundary, falling back to a no-op component if the import fails. The layout and the query-client provider now only render these loaders.
steps: Start at `web/app/layout.tsx`: the root layout renders `<ReactScanLoader />` at the top of `<body>`, replacing the old direct `<ReactScan />`.
`devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx` checks `IS_DEV`, then lazily imports `./scan` and shows a text fallback while the chunk loads; on import failure it logs to the console and renders nothing.
`devtools/react-scan/scan.tsx` (moved unchanged) calls `scan({ dangerouslyForceRunInProduction: true })` in a `useEffect`.
`web/context/query-client.tsx` now renders `<TanStackDevtoolsLoader />` inside `QueryClientProvider`, before `children` (it used to come after).
`devtools/tanstack/loader.tsx` uses the same IS_DEV → lazy → Suspense pattern with a `null` fallback, and lazily imports `./devtools` (`TanStackDevtoolsWrapper`, moved unchanged).

findings.title: React Scan Suspense fallback shows a visible placeholder in body
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx` line 20, the Suspense fallback renders a visible "Loading devtools..." div at the top of <body> during dev page loads, even though the lazily loaded ReactScan component renders null. Change the fallback to `null` to match `web/app/components/devtools/tanstack/loader.tsx`.

findings.title: TanStack loader silently swallows import failures
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/devtools/tanstack/loader.tsx` lines 9-11, the `.catch` on the lazy import discards the error silently. Log it with `console.error('Failed to load TanStack devtools:', error)` before returning the null component, matching the pattern in `web/app/components/devtools/react-scan/loader.tsx` lines 9-12.

findings.title: PR describes a devtools/index.ts barrel that isn't in the change
findings.fixPrompt: The PR description mentions `web/app/components/devtools/index.ts` barrel exports, but the file doesn't exist. Either create `web/app/components/devtools/index.ts` that re-exports only `ReactScanLoader` and `TanStackDevtoolsLoader` from the two `loader.tsx` files (do NOT re-export `scan.tsx` or `devtools.tsx`, because that would defeat lazy loading), and update `web/app/layout.tsx` line 11 and `web/context/query-client.tsx` line 5 to import from it, or update the PR description to match the code.
